title: Chern Insulators on a Twisted Klein Bottle
abstract: Recently, momentum-space nonsymmorphic symmetries have attracted considerable attention. However, their realizations typically rely on fine-tuning hopping phases to satisfy the required projective symmetry algebras. Here, we show that such symmetry algebras arise naturally on bipartite lattices through the interplay of crystalline and sublattice symmetries. Unlike previously studied cases, these symmetry operators can anticommute with the Hamiltonian and are therefore referred to as momentum-space nonsymmorphic chiral symmetries. Although the free actions of these symmetries reduce the Brillouin torus to more elementary manifolds, the resulting manifolds are twisted in the Atiyah--Segal formalism. In particular, chiral glide reflection (screw rotation) gives rise to a twisted Klein bottle (dicosm) in two (three) dimensions, and this twisting dramatically alters the topological classification. Unlike the untwisted Klein bottle, whose nonorientability forces the Chern number to vanish, the twisted Klein bottle can host nonzero Chern numbers, corresponding to even Chern numbers on the torus. At open boundaries, the corresponding topological invariant manifests itself through chiral edge states exhibiting a glide-reflection structure in energy--momentum space. Our results establish momentum-space nonsymmorphic chiral symmetry as a new organizing principle for discovering and engineering topological phases beyond conventional crystalline classifications.
summary: This work introduces momentum-space nonsymmorphic chiral symmetry as a novel organizing principle for topological materials. By analyzing systems on twisted manifolds like the Klein bottle, the authors show that this symmetry allows for the existence of nonzero Chern numbers, which are constrained to be even integers. This provides a new theoretical framework for engineering topological phases and predicting robust edge states.
main_problem: To establish momentum-space nonsymmorphic chiral symmetry as a new organizing principle for discovering and engineering topological phases beyond conventional crystalline classifications.
main_result: The presence of a twisted Klein bottle manifold, arising from chiral glide reflection, allows for nonzero Chern numbers, unlike the untwisted case, and this symmetry constrains the total Chern number to be an even integer.
method: The analysis uses topological classification via twisted K-groups and computes the Chern number using flux integrals over the Brillouin torus.
model_or_system: The study analyzes bipartite lattices exhibiting momentum-space nonsymmorphic symmetries, specifically chiral glide reflection and chiral twofold screw rotation, which are realized through the interplay of crystalline and sublattice symmetries.
key_observables: Nonzero, even Chern numbers ($C_K$), and chiral edge states exhibiting a glide-reflection structure in energy-momentum space.
important_parameters: The symmetry operators anticommute with the Hamiltonian, and the topological invariant depends critically on the twisting $	au \in H^1(M, \mathbb{Z}_2)$.
main_assumptions: The mechanism is limited to producing factor systems valued in $\{\pm 1\}$, restricting the achievable screw rotation to a twofold rotation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the momentum space reduction to a Klein bottle/dicosm and the edge gluing rules. Figure 2 shows the band structure for an SHO lattice model, detailing Berry-phase flow and edge states.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the concept of momentum-space nonsymmorphic chiral symmetry, derives the symmetry operators for specific lattices, calculates the topological invariant using twisted K-theory, and applies this framework to specific models (2D and 3D) to demonstrate nontrivial topology.
why_interesting: The concept of momentum-space nonsymmorphic chiral symmetry provides a powerful, symmetry-based tool to predict and classify topological phases in condensed matter systems, extending beyond standard crystalline symmetries.
